# Aunt Euphemia

## Overview

- **Age:** Elderly  <sub>[v2 c19 P11](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0011), [v2 c27 P5](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0005)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c19 P11](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0011)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper at Tabby's Place  <sub>[v2 c26 P13](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0013)</sub>
- **Titles:** Aunt Euphemia  <sub>[v2 c26 P13](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0013)</sub>; Aunt Phemie  <sub>[v2 c26 P13](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0013)</sub>; Aunty J.  <sub>[v2 c24 P5](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Euphemia is a small, elderly woman with a gently triangular face, rose-colored cheeks, and large, tender blue eyes. She has silver-white hair arranged in charming small rolls above her ears, and wrinkled hands.

_Sources: [v2 c19 P11](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0011), [v2 c21 P51](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0051)_

## Personality

Aunt Euphemia is cheerful, indulgent, and youthful at heart, possessing a keen sense of humor. She prefers to let young women manage their own affairs rather than supervise or lecture them. Warm and hospitable, she is an excellent cook and housekeeper who takes delight in life's simple pleasures.

_Sources: [v2 c19 P11](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0011), [v2 c21 P13](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0013), [v2 c21 P51](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0051), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002)_

## Traits

- Youthful at heart  <sub>[v2 c19 P11](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0011), [v2 c27 P1](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0001)</sub>
- Indulgent and non-judgmental  <sub>[v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c26 P16](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0016)</sub>
- Sense of humor  <sub>[v2 c21 P51](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0051)</sub>

## Abilities

- Excellent cooking and housekeeping skills  <sub>[v2 c21 P13](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0013), [v2 c26 P13](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0013)</sub>
- Fine needlework and knitting  <sub>[v2 c20 P0](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0000), [v2 c21 P13](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0013)</sub>

## Goals

- Keep house for Mabel Colby, Nell Harcourt, Honora Hollis, and Cressida Lindsay at Tabby's Place  <sub>[v2 c26 P13](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0013)</sub>

## History

After her daughter married and left for the foreign mission field in India, Aunt Euphemia was left alone in a large house. Mabel Colby suggested that Aunt Euphemia move to Portmaris to act as housekeeper for her, Nell Harcourt, Honora Hollis, and Cressida Lindsay at Tabby's Place. She moved in during the autumn, bringing along her two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, as well as adopting the stray cat Smudge. She spent her days managing the household, knitting, and enjoying the lively company of the student boarders. When the girls departed for their summer vacations, Aunt Euphemia stayed behind at Tabby's Place to care for the house and cats. She remained to manage the house for a second year when the lease was extended.

_Sources: [v2 c16 P12](../source/v02-c16.md#nw-v02-c16-p0012), [v2 c26 P13](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0013), [v3 c10 P7](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0007)_

## Background by volume

- Named Jamesina after her father James, who drowned at sea shortly before her birth  <sub>[v2 c21 P13](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0013)</sub>
- Her single daughter married and departed for the foreign mission field in India  <sub>[v2 c26 P13](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0013), [v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025)</sub>

## Quotes

> You are able to speak equally well at a later time. My rule when I was a girl was work before play.  <sub>[v2 c25 P3](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0003)</sub>

> I will not. If you will ever understand how to conduct yourselves, you are at an age to know it now. Therefore, as it pertains to me, you are all free to ruin yourselves as you see fit.  <sub>[v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053)</sub>

> It is quite an outmoded method, but I am outmoded myself. My garments are, and naturally my views are as well. Remember, I am not claiming they are superior because of it.  <sub>[v2 c21 P13](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0013)</sub>

> Don't worry. Thank goodness we still don't have to pay for air and salvation  <sub>[v2 c24 P4](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0004)</sub>

> Ah, it seems to me that everyone asks in prayer for certain outcomes that are actually undesired, provided we possess sufficient honesty to examine our inner selves.  <sub>[v3 c35 P15](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0015)</sub>
